page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.large is an x86_64 architecture compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, and is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.c6a.large exhibits modest performance characteristics. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, along with Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth for read-only operations is limited, placing in the bottom 10%, while write bandwidth for large blocks registers in the bottom 25%. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, as well as Geekbench single-core processing.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a dedicated CPU allocation with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, aligning with compute-optimized profiles. However, the low memory capacity and lack of local storage present clear tradeoffs, restricting its utility for memory-intensive or high-I/O workloads. Given its lower-tier benchmark results in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, the instance is positioned as a budget-friendly entry point for lightweight compute tasks rather than high-throughput production environments.

The ecs.c6a.large is best suited for low-intensity workloads that require dedicated CPU execution but do not demand high memory or storage performance. Appropriate use cases include basic single-threaded processing, lightweight utility scripting, simple CI/CD tasks, and low-traffic web serving.
